feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning and a coherent career progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows breadth across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia, but it would be stronger with tighter formatting, fewer repeated themes, and more outcome-focused evidence.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear narrative of progression from coordinator to director to consultant, which supports credibility and leadership growth.  
- Strong scope and specificity in digital work: Drupal migration, 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, analytics stack, studio buildout.  
- Writing is polished and generally consistent, with a confident tone aligned to communications and strategy roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact beyond scope: include outcomes such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication across Summary, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“workflows, and systems” vs other lists); standardize punctuation in bullets and section naming. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less repetition of skills already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and tighten the opening: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs.”
- Add a clearer senior-value statement tied to recent roles: mention enterprise web modernization, digital governance, analytics, or mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace generic phrases like “expert in” and “strong background in” with sharper, outcome-oriented wording.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and the workflows and systems that enable coordinated communications at scale. Brings deep experience in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflows and systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat heavily from Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- Avoid adding platform/tool detail here; those are already well covered in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership/technical strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication”; “Web platform modernization” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Group related items and reduce repetition around workflows/systems. Suggested version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS management • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, reporting & insight generation • Workflow automation & systems design • Stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Keep style consistent: use plural nouns where appropriate (“communications,” “systems”) and parallel phrasing throughout.
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: strategy, web/platforms, analytics, governance, then multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Workflow design/systems architecture” and several technical items duplicate Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo director entry. Tighten it around consultant-specific scope, senior advisory value, and any new initiatives since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, and cross-channel content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and emphasize distinct consulting work: AI-enabled search, microsite/storytelling architecture, governance, and technical implementation.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/templates/toolkits launched, workflow efficiencies, search improvements, stakeholder groups supported, or traffic/user adoption.
- Example rewrite: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform optimization, and communications operations; built microsite and modular content frameworks, improved cross-channel workflows and analytics, delivered front-end/CMS enhancements for public web properties, and led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval strategy, structured content, and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current references to workflows, analytics, governance, and Drupal improvements repeat the 2022–2024 director role.
- “Large public-facing web properties” is vague; use scale or outcome instead.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/enterprise scope, and the biggest differentiators versus the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine channel oversight bullets and add outcomes where possible: email engagement growth, social growth, production volume, cost savings, faster publishing, or reporting adoption.
- Rewrite the website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make the studio/analytics bullets more results-led: note reduced vendor reliance, expanded event capacity, improved reporting speed, or better executive decision-making.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Recurring multimedia content/video as a channel” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and infrastructure.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears in the current consultant role; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel growth, and editorial operations rather than broad platform ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to focus on role level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-channel editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director role’s opening.
- “Helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel” overlaps with the earlier role’s “weekly video updates.”

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad terms like “multi-channel communications leadership” and “audience-focused content planning” with more executive, differentiated language tied to recent work.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance, publishing standards & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Stakeholder alignment and audience-centered content planning
- If space allows, use “content operations” or “platform governance” to better reflect your 2022–present leadership scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “multi-channel communication” already appear in the header/core competencies; rephrase to avoid repetition.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is close to “Policy & advocacy communication” elsewhere; consider keeping only one version.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo work, but it reads as a raw keyword list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. Make it more selective and outcome-oriented so it reinforces recent impact rather than repeating tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as grouped capabilities, not a software dump: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • SharePoint / WordPress / Power Pages • AI-enabled search”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first; they are most supported by recent experience.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer value language if possible: “Web platforms & digital systems” or “CMS platforms & technical delivery.”
- If space allows, add one light qualifier tied to impact: “supporting large public-facing sites, modular content systems, and streamlined publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave specific tools like GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, Zapier, etc. in Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies/Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for your most recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory. Tighten it around decision-making impact and use broader phrasing so it complements—not repeats—your Director role bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability statement: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery for KPI design, executive reporting, and digital performance optimization.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive reporting” or “decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider “search, SEO, and conversion/performance analysis” if optimization work included user journeys beyond SEO alone.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented phrase: “analytics infrastructure and dashboards that improved strategic decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with the Director of Digital Media bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure; avoid repeating the exact tool sequence elsewhere.
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies, so this section should emphasize specificity or outcomes, not restate the same idea.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with stronger evidence already shown in recent NACo roles. Make it more senior, specific, and aligned to the studio/build-out and event delivery impact in 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with higher-value wording tied to scope:  
  “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows • Post-production editing”
- If space allows, emphasize leadership/ownership over task execution:  
  “In-house studio operations and live production”
- Consider combining related items for concision: merge “Livestreaming” + “Hybrid and virtual event production.”
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add scale language such as “broadcast-quality” or “multi-camera” rather than listing only tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; keep one broader and one more specific.
- “Video production and editing” is already evidenced in multiple NACo roles, so avoid repeating low-detail wording.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since recent roles emphasize Drupal-led modernization, this item should signal depth and relevance, not just names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of bare tools: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it is materially relevant to target roles; it reads lighter than the rest.
- Keep naming consistent with the CV’s impact language: prioritize platforms tied to modernization, publishing operations, and public-facing web properties.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- “Web & CMS administration” also appears in Core Competencies, so this item should add specificity or be consolidated.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and slightly more senior to match recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add level/scope language instead of more tools: Front-end implementation, tag management, lightweight serverless scripting, and deployment workflow support
- If space allows, prioritize tools tied to recent work and outcomes, e.g. Drupal front-end implementation, API integrations, GTM configuration, Cloudflare Workers scripting

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” “Workflow automation”); consider trimming one version.
- GitHub Actions may also overlap conceptually with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep it here only if you’ve used it for code/deployment workflows specifically.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, not just tools: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Group by function and trim lower-value tools: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- If space allows, add a short qualifier tied to recent work: “Used to build editorial planning, approvals, intake, and cross-team communication workflows.”
- Prioritize strongest/relevant platforms first; consider dropping one or two older/generic PM tools if not used recently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and automation are already mentioned in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them verbatim without adding context.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep only if they were central to workflow design, not just daily communication.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the scale/strategic email work shown in recent NACo roles. Strengthen it by signaling platform depth and audience engagement relevance without repeating work-experience bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers for depth: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation)** • **Higher Logic (member email/community engagement)** • **Mailchimp (newsletter production)**
- Keep this section platform-focused only; let the recent NACo roles carry audience size, newsletter frequency, and leadership impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that already appears in Work Experience.
- Don’t restate “multi-channel communications” or governance language already covered in Core Competencies and recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a fuller version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and standardize publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this item as the launch/early build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this entry more tactical and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed as a foundation role, with more emphasis on outcomes and less overlap with later digital/media positions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more active: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or results: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how content supported member engagement/policy communications.
- Consider reducing generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” in favor of specific outputs or channels.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on research/innovation support plus the first-podcast achievement.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social responsibilities that are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
